label: <DEL> step of long sequences rich in c/d/f/r/x/3
explanation: Mainly a delimiter-step unit: 80% of activation mass is at the <DEL> input (recall_idx 0), but it fires on only about 10% of <DEL> steps. Rate rises steeply with sequence length (L=9 contributes 52% of mass, L<=5 almost nothing) and with how many of c, d, f, r, x, 3 appeared among the original tokens. Weaker spill-over occurs on the last 1-3 original tokens of long sequences (15% of mass, x and o inputs over-represented) and on the first copy step (4%), often in sequences starting with w/g/2/k/b. It never fires at t<3 and is essentially silent in the copy phase after recall_idx 2. Precision stays low even with the length and content conditions (about 0.3), so whatever decides which long-sequence delimiter steps fire is only partly captured. Plain phase==1 gives mass recall 0.80 but precision 0.10.
